title: Redundant Connection
summary: Given a graph that initially forms a tree with n nodes and an additional edge, identify and return an edge that can be removed to restore the graph as a tree with n nodes.
statement: Given a graph that initially forms a tree with n nodes and an additional edge, identify and return an edge that can be removed to restore the graph as a tree with n nodes. If multiple edges meet this criterion, select the one that appears last in the input.
constraints: The edges describe a tree on n nodes plus one extra undirected edge.
Return the last input edge whose removal restores a tree.
hints: The redundant edge is the one whose endpoints are already connected by earlier edges.
Maintain connected components with union-find in input order.
Find both roots; return the edge if equal, otherwise union them.
Before the unique cycle closes, every edge joins components; the closing edge is exactly the removable answer required by input order.
editorial: Before the unique cycle closes, every edge joins components; the closing edge is exactly the removable answer required by input order.

tests.explanation: Adding two-three connects vertices already joined through one.
Edge one-four is the first edge that closes the unique cycle.
